seo.title: Homeless and housing-crisis help in Layton - No Home Help
seo.description: Current Layton and Davis County contacts for shelter routes, food, health care, benefits, jobs, legal help and specialist support.

page.heading: Homeless and housing-crisis help in Layton
page.urgent: Immediate danger, serious injury, overdose, fire or a crime in progress: call 911. Mental-health or substance-use crisis: call or text 988. Community referrals: call 211.
page.notice: Davis County's general warming center opens only on officially activated Code Blue nights. Year-round shelters are regional or serve specific groups. Call before travelling. No listing guarantees a bed, room, housing, appointment, benefit, payment, treatment or job.
page.intro: For a cold-weather night, check the current Davis County Code Blue status first. Families with minor children have a separate Open Doors route. Outside Code Blue, ask Open Doors or 211 about regional shelter in Ogden or Salt Lake County, and state any transport, pet, health, safety or accessibility needs.
page.footer: No Home Help is independent of government and service providers. Information was checked against official provider or government pages; report a change if a number, address or access rule is no longer correct.

entries.title: 911 — emergency services
entries.description: Call for immediate danger, serious injury, suspected overdose, fire or a crime in progress. Give the exact address or nearest intersection and describe the immediate risk.
entries.how_to_access: Call 911. Do not use a shelter or crisis-line number instead when someone needs an ambulance, fire response or immediate police help.

entries.title: Utah 211 — community-service referrals
entries.description: Statewide information and referral for food, housing, health care, transportation, legal help, benefits and other local services. A navigator can search for current Davis County and regional options.
entries.how_to_access: Call 211 or use the online directory. Ask the navigator to confirm eligibility, hours, transport and whether an appointment is required.

entries.title: Davis Behavioral Health — crisis response
entries.description: Local 24-hour mental-health crisis support and mobile response for Davis County. This is not a homeless shelter.
entries.address: Main Street Clinic, 934 S Main Street, Layton, UT 84041
entries.how_to_access: Call the crisis line or call or text 988. Call 911 for immediate danger, serious injury or overdose.

entries.title: Davis County Community Services — Code Blue information
entries.description: County contact for current Code Blue warming-center status, free seasonal bus passes and access questions. A Code Blue shelter is not open every night.
entries.hours: Call for current status; the warming center opens 19:30–07:30 only during an active Code Blue
entries.how_to_access: Check the official page or call before travelling. Ask where to obtain a bus pass and whether the center is active that night.

entries.title: Davis County Warming Center — Code Blue nights only
entries.description: Overnight cots and warmth for unsheltered adults only when Davis County officially activates Code Blue because of extreme cold or weather. It is not a year-round shelter. Pet admission depends on capacity and behaviour, with no more than one animal per household.
entries.address: Talia's Event Center, 22 E 200 S, Clearfield, UT 84015
entries.hours: Active Code Blue nights only, 19:30–07:30, during the seasonal period
entries.how_to_access: Confirm activation before travelling. Adults may arrive at the center; ask the county about free UTA passes. Bring essential medication and disclose any accessibility need.

entries.title: Open Doors — Code Blue rooms for families with minor children
entries.description: Separate non-congregate shelter route for families with children under 18 during an active Davis County Code Blue. Rooms and vouchers are limited and not available as a general year-round shelter.
entries.hours: Call only when Code Blue is active
entries.how_to_access: Call Open Doors and state that minor children are present. Follow the screening instructions and ask what to do if no room remains.

entries.title: Lantern House — regional year-round shelter in Ogden
entries.description: Regional emergency shelter serving adults and families from northern Utah. Davis County identifies Lantern House as a year-round shelter route used by local residents. Capacity and intake rules change.
entries.hours: Call for current intake and availability
entries.how_to_access: Call before travelling from Layton. State whether you are an adult, couple or family and ask about capacity, identification, pets and transport.

entries.title: Ogden Rescue Mission — regional faith-based shelter
entries.description: Regional Christian homeless service center offering shelter, meals, hygiene, clothing and addiction recovery for adults. Space is limited and program expectations vary.
entries.how_to_access: Call before travelling and ask about who can be admitted, check-in time, identification, chapel or program expectations and the next option if full.

entries.title: Safe Harbor Crisis Center — confidential shelter
entries.description: Confidential emergency shelter and advocacy for people affected by domestic violence, sexual assault, stalking or dating violence. Space is arranged through the crisis line.
entries.address: Shelter location is confidential; Lifeline Prevention Center: 223 Larson Lane, Layton, UT 84041
entries.how_to_access: Call from a safe device if possible. Ask about shelter, transport, children, accessibility and pets. Call 911 for immediate danger.

entries.title: Open Doors — Homeless to Housed and prevention
entries.description: Housing case management, rental or deposit assistance, landlord mediation and street outreach for qualifying Davis County households. Funding and eligibility are limited; this is not a guaranteed same-night bed.
entries.how_to_access: Call as early as possible and ask for housing or street-outreach intake. Bring lease, eviction, income or identification information if available.

entries.title: Davis Community Housing Authority — public and voucher housing
entries.description: Public housing and federal voucher programs for qualifying low-income households. Some waiting lists are closed and open lists have long waits; this is not emergency shelter.
entries.how_to_access: Check the current waiting-list status and apply online to an open list. Keep a reliable postal address updated so the application remains active.

entries.title: Open Doors — mobile food bank
entries.description: Emergency food distributed at rotating drive-up and walk-up sites in Layton and nearby Davis County communities. Locations and dates change, and the former Layton warehouse is no longer a regular distribution site.
entries.address: Rotating sites; check the official schedule
entries.how_to_access: Check the official schedule immediately before travelling. Follow the walk-up or drive-up instructions and bring bags when the listing requests them.

entries.title: Utah Food Bank — find another pantry or mobile distribution
entries.description: Official locator for food pantries and mobile distributions in Davis County. Partner sites set their own hours, documents and service limits.
entries.address: Use the official locator for the nearest site
entries.how_to_access: Search by address or ZIP code, then call the chosen site to confirm the next distribution and eligibility.

entries.title: Ogden Rescue Mission — regional meals and food boxes
entries.description: Faith-based regional service offering meals and family food boxes alongside shelter and hygiene services. Serving times and access rules can change.
entries.how_to_access: Call before travelling from Layton and ask about the next meal, food-box requirements and whether chapel attendance is connected to a service.

entries.title: Open Doors — family and self-sufficiency services
entries.description: Community Action provider offering housing help, food, crisis nursery, case management, tax preparation, mentoring and other support for Davis County households. Programs have separate eligibility rules.
entries.how_to_access: Call and describe the most urgent need. Ask which program and location handles it and what documents to bring.

entries.title: Ogden Rescue Mission — regional basic-needs help
entries.description: Christian homeless service center with shelter, meals, hygiene, clothing, food boxes and addiction recovery. Some activities are faith-based; ask what participation is expected for the service you need.
entries.how_to_access: Call before travelling from Layton and ask about current service hours and requirements.

entries.title: Ogden Rescue Mission — regional hygiene services
entries.description: The regional homeless service center lists hygiene among its basic services. Access times and supplies can change.
entries.how_to_access: Call before travelling and ask whether showers or hygiene supplies are open to non-shelter guests that day.

entries.title: Ogden Rescue Mission — regional clothing help
entries.description: Donated clothing for people using the regional homeless service center. Stock and sizes depend on donations.
entries.how_to_access: Call before travelling and ask about referral or guest requirements and the specific item or size needed.

entries.title: Midtown Community Health Center of Davis — medical and dental
entries.description: Community clinic providing primary medical and dental care for patients of all ages, including acute and chronic care. Ask about insurance, sliding-fee eligibility and appointment availability.
entries.address: 22 S State Street, Suite 1007, Clearfield, UT 84015
entries.hours: Medical and dental Monday–Friday 07:30–18:00; second Tuesday opens 09:00; dental lunch closure 13:00–14:00
entries.how_to_access: Call for an appointment and ask about fees and same-day availability. Call 911 for a life-threatening emergency.

entries.title: Davis Behavioral Health — mental health and substance-use services
entries.description: Community mental-health provider offering assessment, therapy, psychiatric care, case management and substance-use treatment for qualifying residents. Eligibility, fees and wait times vary.
entries.hours: Call for outpatient hours; crisis support is available 24 hours
entries.how_to_access: Call for intake and explain insurance or Medicaid status. For immediate crisis use 801-614-2829 or 988.

entries.title: 988 Utah — crisis counselling and mobile response
entries.description: Immediate support for suicide, mental-health or substance-use crises, with connection to local mobile response or a receiving center when appropriate.
entries.how_to_access: Call or text 988. Call 911 for immediate danger, serious injury or overdose.

entries.title: Davis County Library — Layton Branch
entries.description: Public indoor space with toilets, seating, information help, Wi-Fi, internet computers, photocopying and scanning. Library rules apply and it is not an overnight shelter.
entries.how_to_access: Walk in during opening hours. Ask staff about guest computer access and local service information.

entries.title: Layton Branch Library — public internet and Wi-Fi
entries.description: Public internet computers, Wi-Fi, scanning and photocopying. Session limits and printing or copying charges may apply.
entries.how_to_access: Ask staff for a guest computer session, Wi-Fi or charging. Protect passwords and personal information on public devices.

entries.title: UTA Reduced Fare FAREPAY Card
entries.description: Reduced fares for qualifying low-income riders, people with disabilities, seniors and youth. Approval and identity or eligibility evidence are required.
entries.address: Apply online; nearest full customer-service options include Ogden Transit Center
entries.how_to_access: Apply online or call for the nearest in-person option. During Code Blue, ask Davis County about free 24-hour passes to the warming center.

entries.title: Davis County Code Blue — free seasonal bus passes
entries.description: During Code Blue season the county provides free 24-hour UTA passes to help people travel to and from the warming center. Availability is tied to the seasonal response.
entries.address: Passes at the warming center or through Davis County Community Services
entries.how_to_access: Call Community Services or ask at the warming center. Confirm the current route and activation before travelling.

entries.title: Utah Workforce Services — SNAP, medical and cash assistance
entries.description: Applications and eligibility support for SNAP, medical, financial and child-care assistance at the nearby Clearfield employment center or online.
entries.how_to_access: Apply through myCase, by telephone or in person. The initial SNAP application can be submitted before every verification document is available.

entries.title: Utah Workforce Services — Clearfield employment center
entries.description: Job search, employment counselling and possible training or education support for eligible jobseekers. Services do not guarantee employment.
entries.hours: Call for current lobby and appointment hours
entries.how_to_access: Apply online or visit the center. Ask for help creating an account and explain if transport, internet or identification is a barrier.

entries.title: Open Doors — self-sufficiency case management
entries.description: Case management and mentoring focused on housing stability, employment and long-term self-reliance. Program enrollment and openings vary.
entries.how_to_access: Call and ask which case-management or mentoring program is accepting participants.

entries.title: Utah Legal Services — Ogden civil legal aid
entries.description: Free civil legal help for eligible low-income Utah residents, including some housing, public-benefit, family and consumer matters. Representation is not guaranteed.
entries.hours: Public office Tuesday–Thursday 09:00–15:00; additional hours by appointment
entries.how_to_access: Apply online or call intake before travelling from Layton. Explain any eviction, hearing or filing deadline immediately.

entries.title: Safe Harbor Crisis Center — 24-hour helpline
entries.description: Confidential crisis support, safety planning, advocacy and emergency shelter for people affected by domestic violence, rape, sexual assault, stalking or dating violence.
entries.address: Lifeline Prevention Center: 223 Larson Lane, Layton, UT 84041; shelter location is confidential
entries.how_to_access: Call from a safe device if possible. Ask about shelter, safe transport, children, accessibility and pets. Call 911 for immediate danger.

entries.title: Open Doors — Davis County street outreach
entries.description: Outreach workers look for and connect people experiencing literal homelessness with shelter information, housing case management and other resources.
entries.how_to_access: Call with a clear location and describe the person's immediate needs. Call 911 instead for immediate danger or a medical emergency.

entries.title: Open Doors — crisis nursery and family support
entries.description: Short-term safe care for children while a parent handles a crisis, appointment or essential task. This is not ordinary day care and scheduling is required.
entries.how_to_access: Call extension 0 to schedule and complete required paperwork. Explain any urgent family or housing crisis.

entries.title: VA — homeless veteran help
entries.description: VA help for veterans who are homeless or at risk, including shelter and housing referrals, health care, benefits, employment support and justice-system re-entry. Northern Utah is served through the Salt Lake City VA region.
entries.how_to_access: Call the national line or 801-582-1565 extension 2746. You do not need to prove eligibility before making the first call.

entries.title: Davis County Warming Center — limited pet access
entries.description: During an active Code Blue, the warming center may allow one animal per household depending on capacity and animal behaviour. Admission is not guaranteed.
entries.how_to_access: Call before arrival and describe the animal. Ask what supplies or restraint are required and request a backup option if the animal cannot be admitted.

entries.title: Ruff Haven — regional temporary pet crisis care
entries.description: Salt Lake-based short-term shelter or foster care for dogs and cats when an owner faces a qualifying crisis. This is a regional option and acceptance and transport are not guaranteed.
entries.address: Salt Lake City area; intake arranged after approval
entries.how_to_access: Apply online and explain the crisis, pet and transport situation. Ask Open Doors or Safe Harbor about nearer pet-safe options first.

entries.title: Davis County — current Code Blue page
entries.description: Official activation criteria, current warming-center address, seasonal hours, transport help, family route and pet policy. Check it each time because Code Blue services are not open nightly.
entries.how_to_access: Check the activation notice or call the county before travelling to the warming center.
